source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps synagogue exclusion, lethal persecution, future hour, and killers’ mistaken religious service.
key_decisions.before: They will put you out of the synagogues. In fact, an hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think they are offering service to God.
key_decisions.after: They will expel you from the synagogues. In fact, an hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think they are offering worship to God.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: They will put you out of the synagogues; indeed, an hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think that he is offering service to God.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves return to the sender and Jesus’ observation despite earlier questions in another conversational moment.
key_decisions.before: “But now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’
key_decisions.after: But now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves truth claim, advantage, necessary departure, Advocate, and Jesus’ sending.
key_decisions.before: But I tell you the truth: it is better for you that I go away. For if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you.
key_decisions.after: Nevertheless, I tell you the truth: it is better for you that I go away. For if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go away; for if I do not go away, the Helper will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.

key_decisions.rationale: Renders the verb’s range as expose and preserves the three subjects of the Spirit’s case against the world.
key_decisions.before: When he comes, he will expose the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment:
key_decisions.after: And when he comes, he will expose the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment:
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And when that one comes, he will convict the world concerning sin and concerning righteousness and concerning judgment:

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves the stated reason, destination, and end of visible presence.
key_decisions.before: concerning righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you will no longer see me;
key_decisions.after: concerning righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you will see me no longer;
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: concerning righteousness, because I go to the Father and you no longer see me;

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps personal agency, title, comprehensive guidance, dependent speech, hearing, and future disclosure.
key_decisions.before: When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth. For he will not speak from himself, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will announce to you the things that are coming.
key_decisions.after: But when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all the truth. For he will not speak on his own, but will speak whatever he hears, and he will announce to you what is to come.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: But when that one comes, the Spirit of truth, he will guide you into all the truth; for he will not speak from himself, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will declare to you the things that are coming.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the gender-specific embodied comparison, appointed hour, anguish, joy, birth, and world.
key_decisions.before: When a woman gives birth, she has sorrow because her hour has come. But when she has given birth to the child, she no longer remembers the distress because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.
key_decisions.after: When a woman is giving birth, she has pain because her hour has come. But when the child is born, she no longer remembers the anguish because of her joy that a human being has been born into the world.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: When a woman is giving birth, she has sorrow because her hour has come; but when she has given birth to the child, she no longer remembers the distress, because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps the distinction between questioning Jesus and requesting from the Father, with double amen and Jesus’ name.
key_decisions.before: “On that day you will ask me nothing. Truly, truly, I tell you, whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you.
key_decisions.after: On that day you will not ask me anything. Truly, truly, I tell you: whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And in that day you will ask me nothing. Truly, truly, I say to you, whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give to you.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves future asking and the carefully limited statement about Jesus’ intercession.
key_decisions.before: On that day you will ask in my name. I am not telling you that I will ask the Father for you,
key_decisions.after: On that day you will ask in my name. I am not telling you that I will ask the Father on your behalf,
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: In that day you will ask in my name, and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father on your behalf;

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves imminent and present hour, individual scattering, abandonment, and the Father’s presence.
key_decisions.before: Look—an hour is coming, and has come, when you will be scattered, each to your own place, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
key_decisions.after: Look, an hour is coming—and has come—when each of you will be scattered to your own home and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: Behold, an hour is coming, and has come, when you will be scattered each to his own and will leave me alone; and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps purpose, location of peace, real affliction, command for courage, and Jesus’ victory.
key_decisions.before: I have told you these things so that in me you may have peace. In the world you have distress. But take courage: I have overcome the world.”
key_decisions.after: I have told you these things so that in me you may have peace. In the world you have affliction. But take courage: I have overcome the world.”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: These things I have spoken to you so that in me you may have peace. In the world you have tribulation; but take courage, I have overcome the world.”
